notes:
Summary: Cobalt Provisioning Group is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for productionizing a low-latency reranking + embeddings stack used in fraud-scoring and support routing. Primary drivers: predictable throughput for business SLAs, lower per-token unit costs vs hosted, and VPC isolation for PII-sensitive payloads.

POC & requirements (shorthand):
- Workload: mixed traffic: 60% embeddings indexing + similarity queries (batch heavy), 30% reranking (real-time, p95 target), 10% chat ops/alerts.
- Latency targets: reranking p95 <= 80ms (512-token context), chat interactive p95 <= 150ms.
- Throughput baseline: 1,200 small requests/sec (avg), peak 3,000 reqs/sec during batch windows; embeddings indexing 200k vectors/day.
- Model prefs: open Llama-3-like variants and a trimmed 70B for reranker; need quantization guidance (int8) and compatibility with Redwood Optimize recommendations.

Cost model notes from 2026-02-18 workshop (internal CRO math):
- Two committed scenarios shown to customer: 
  1) 8x H100 reserved (baseline): estimated monthly commit $180k. Assumed utilization 65% steady-state. Effective unit economics: ~$0.00042 per input+output token at 65% util (model: 70B int8 with optimized kernels). Break-even vs hosted API assumed at ~28% sustained utilization.
  2) 16x A100 reserved (scale-forward): estimated monthly commit $260k. Assumed utilization 55% (lower due to bursts). Effective unit economics: ~$0.00036 per token at 55% util after autoscaling & batching improvements.
- Sensitivity: each 5ppt drop in utilization increases unit cost ~8-10%. Prefix/KV caching expected to reduce computed tokens by ~12-18% for reranker flows.
- SLA implications: Redwood proposed 99.9% uptime for Dedicated with p95 latency SLOs tied to model family and sequence length buckets; customer expects financial remedies for SLO misses and a 30-day performance warranty for rollout.

Customer quotes (paraphrased):
- 'We need predictable dollar-per-token that doesn't swing with sudden traffic — CFO will not accept large bill spikes.'
- 'If Redwood can guarantee 80ms p95 for reranking under our 3k peak, procurement will prefer committed capacity.'

Open technical items / ask list for Redwood:
- Provide formal committed-capacity pricing sheet with modeled tiers (4/8/16 GPU configs) and per-token breakouts at 40/60/80% util.
- Confirm int8 quantization recommendations and perf delta vs fp16 for our 70B model family.
- Draft Dedicated SLA with clear latency SLO mapping, credits matrix, and maintenance windows.
- Network egress and VPC peering runbook + estimated monthly egress costs.
- Run a short bench: simulate 3k concurrent small rerank requests against proposed 8x H100 pool (record results).

Next steps (from AE notes): finalize a 2-week capacity-sizing workshop, deliver revised pricing with 3 utilization scenarios, legal to review SLA template, target procurement decision by 2026-05.
